question.nlq: Hey there! So I've been thinking about my favorite superheroes and I'm super curious - can you help me find all the heroes whose strength stat is actually higher than the average strength of all heroes from their SAME publisher? Oh, and I'd also like to know how many unique superpowers each of these strong heroes has! Could you show me their superhero name, publisher name, actual strength value, their power count, AND rank them within their publisher group so I can see who's the top dog in terms of raw strength from each company? Make sure to only include those who have AT LEAST 3 superpowers too. Pretty please?

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH strength_records AS (
    SELECT 
        s.id as hero_id,
        s.superhero_name,
        p.publisher_name,
        s.publisher_id,
        ha.attribute_value as strength
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute attr ON ha.attribute_id = attr.id AND attr.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
avg_strength_per_publisher AS (
    SELECT 
        publisher_name,
        AVG(strength) as avg_strength
    FROM strength_records
    GROUP BY publisher_name
),
power_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) as power_count
    FROM hero_power
    GROUP BY hero_id
),
ranked_heroes AS (
    SELECT 
        sr.hero_id,
        sr.superhero_name,
        sr.publisher_name,
        sr.strength,
        pc.power_count,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sr.publisher_id ORDER BY sr.strength DESC) as strength_rank
    FROM strength_records sr
    JOIN power_counts pc ON sr.hero_id = pc.hero_id
    JOIN avg_strength_per_publisher avp ON sr.publisher_name = avp.publisher_name
    WHERE sr.strength > avp.avg_strength
      AND pc.power_count >= 3
)
SELECT 
    superhero_name,
    publisher_name,
    strength,
    power_count,
    strength_rank
FROM ranked_heroes
ORDER BY publisher_name, strength_rank

WITH strength_per_hero AS (
    SELECT s.id AS hero_id,
           s.superhero_name,
           s.publisher_id,
           ha.attribute_value AS strength
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
publisher_avg AS (
    SELECT publisher_id,
           AVG(strength) AS avg_strength
    FROM strength_per_hero
    GROUP BY publisher_id
),
power_count AS (
    SELECT hero_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) AS power_cnt
    FROM hero_power
    GROUP BY hero_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) >= 3
)
SELECT sh.superhero_name,
       p.publisher_name,
       sh.strength,
       pc.power_cnt,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sh.publisher_id ORDER BY sh.strength DESC) AS strength_rank
FROM strength_per_hero sh
JOIN publisher_avg pa ON sh.publisher_id = pa.publisher_id
JOIN publisher p ON sh.publisher_id = p.id
JOIN power_count pc ON sh.hero_id = pc.hero_id
WHERE sh.strength > pa.avg_strength
ORDER BY sh.publisher_id, strength_rank;

WITH strength_data AS (
    SELECT
        s.id AS hero_id,
        s.superhero_name,
        s.publisher_id,
        p.publisher_name,
        ha.attribute_value AS strength,
        COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS power_count
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id AND a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
    LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON s.id = hp.hero_id
    GROUP BY s.id, s.superhero_name, s.publisher_id, p.publisher_name, ha.attribute_value
),
avg_strength AS (
    SELECT
        s.publisher_id,
        AVG(ha.attribute_value) AS avg_strength
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id AND a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
    GROUP BY s.publisher_id
),
filtered AS (
    SELECT
        sd.*,
        a.avg_strength
    FROM strength_data sd
    JOIN avg_strength a ON sd.publisher_id = a.publisher_id
    WHERE sd.strength > a.avg_strength
      AND sd.power_count >= 3
)
SELECT
    superhero_name,
    publisher_name,
    strength,
    power_count,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY publisher_name ORDER BY strength DESC) AS strength_rank
FROM filtered
ORDER BY publisher_name, strength_rank;

WITH strength_attr AS (

question.nlq: Hey! Could you help me pull up the two tallest male superheroes for each alignment? I'd love to see their names, their alignment, how tall they are (cm), and which publisher they're from.

meanings.gt_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT s.superhero_name, a.alignment, s.height_cm, p.publisher_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.id ORDER BY s.height_cm DESC) AS rn FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id JOIN alignment AS a ON s.alignment_id = a.id JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.height_cm IS NOT NULL) SELECT superhero_name, alignment, height_cm, publisher_name FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 2 ORDER BY alignment, rn;
